findings.title: No upper bound on window size before allocating the software surface
findings.message: Window dimensions are checked only for being positive integers. There is no upper bound, even though the config bounds every other resource. A very large integral width or height reaches `RunManual` and the software compositor, which allocate an image of that size and can cause an out-of-memory failure.
findings.suggestion: Add a maximum window dimension, or a total-pixel cap, to `ManualConfig` and enforce it here.

findings.title: Quadratic lookup of accessibility nodes per element
findings.message: For every control, `collect` linearly scans every accessibility node. Capture cost is O(controls × nodes), and the configuration allows up to 65536 controls. Capture runs on each frame during Step and Frame, so large windows can make replay very slow.
findings.suggestion: Build a `map[string]*accessNode` keyed by DomainID once, before `collect`, and look controls up in it.

findings.title: Unchecked type assertion can panic during capture
findings.message: The code asserts `r.widget` to `*core.TextField` whenever `r.node.Kind == ui.TextField`. If reconcile ever backs that kind with another widget type, such as a disabled or read-only variant, the assertion panics inside `owner.Do` during capture. The earlier block already handles the checked case, so this one is also redundant.
findings.suggestion: Use the checked form `field, ok := r.widget.(*core.TextField)` and skip the branch when `ok` is false, or remove the duplicate block.

finding.title: Repeat-click timer drops AsyncLock safety checks in non-manual mode
finding.message: The repeat-click timer callback no longer uses rw.AsyncLock/AsyncUnlock on the non-manual path. It now locks the render context directly. That drops the post-lock check that the widget was not deleted while waiting for the lock. It also drops the sceneUpdating flag set and cleared around the callout. The only liveness check (`tree.IsNil(em.repeatClick)`) runs before the lock is taken. The production path can therefore send Click to a widget deleted in that window. It also skips the scene-updating bookkeeping other code relies on.
finding.suggestion: Keep rw.AsyncLock()/rw.AsyncUnlock() on the non-manual path. Use the direct ownership shortcut only when rc.manual != nil. Re-check widget liveness after acquiring the lock in both modes.

finding.title: Ignored SendDeferred error silently loses timer and leaks credit
finding.message: The error from SendDeferred is discarded inside the clock callback. If admission fails, the timer stays in state 0 and keeps its credit in m.timers. Its callback never runs and no manual failure is recorded. The caller sees a silently lost deadline. Repeated failures also exhaust EventCapacity credits that nothing releases until the window retires.
finding.suggestion: Check the returned error. On failure, call m.fail(err) and retire the timer: set state 3 and delete it from m.timers under m.mu.

finding.title: Manual timer refusal is ignored in Complete.Show and popup timeout
finding.message: The result of scene.afterEvent is stored or discarded without checking for a refusal. Scene.ManualAfterFunc shows that afterEvent can return nil on capacity, lifetime or failure. In that case the completion is silently never shown, and nothing is recorded through ManualFailure. The popup timeout path in popupstage.go has the same problem: the popup would never auto-dismiss and the failure would go unreported. This breaks the checked-refusal behaviour the rest of the patch is built around.
finding.suggestion: In manual mode use `scene.ManualAfterFunc(wait, callback)`. On error call `scene.ManualFailure(err)` and leave delayTimer nil. Apply the same change to the popup timeout in popupstage.go.

finding.title: Unchecked interface type assertion in RequestFrame can panic
finding.message: The unchecked type assertion panics if the system window does not implement RequestPaint(). A panic here would escape a public API that is meant to return an error. The offscreen test driver implements it, but the manual-window contract does not guarantee that every driver does.
finding.suggestion: Use the comma-ok form, for example `p, ok := m.window.SystemWindow.(interface{ RequestPaint() }); if !ok { return ErrManualUnsupported }; p.RequestPaint()`.

finding.title: MonitorOutput silently swallows BeginAmbientWork errors, including nil Lines
finding.message: BeginAmbientWork returns ErrManualExecution when ob.Lines is nil, and MonitorOutput swallows every error and returns. Output monitoring then silently does nothing for a nil Lines, and the caller never learns that the reader was not consumed. Previously this was a loud nil-pointer failure. The manual-refusal case is reported through the Failure callback, but this nil path is not reported anywhere.
finding.suggestion: Distinguish a nil Lines (programmer error) from a manual refusal. For example, check ob.Lines == nil up front and panic or log, and only return silently on ErrManualAmbient.
